newsitem.title: MEXICO: Guatemala goverment, rebels said in new agreement.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala goverment, rebels said in new agreement.

text.p: Guatemala's government and leftist rebels reached a major agreement on Monday on military curbs, setting the stage for a full peace accord by yearend, the Mexican state news agency Notimex reported.

After more than three months of negotiations on the thorny issue of "Strengthening Civil Society and The Role of the Army in a Democratic Society," it said the two sides put the finishing touches on an agreement early on Monday and planned to sign it in Mexico City on Thursday.

The agreement marked the final thematic issue to be discussed as part of a peace agreement that has been negotiated in steps since 1991. Between now and the end of the year, when both sides say they can reach a full peace accord, the discussions will switch to operational difficulties such as drawing the guerrillas back into civilian life in Guatemala and agreeing on a full ceasefire.

"They reached a total accord," Jean Arnault, the United Nations mediator, was quoted by Notimex as saying. He could not immediately be reached by Reuters and the U.N. offices in Mexico were closed for Independence Day celebrations.
The peace talks were held in a Mexico City hotel.

"It's a decisive step toward achieving peace," Guatemalan government negotiator Gustavo Porras told the Mexican news agency. Guerrilla leaders of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit also hailed it.

The war in Guatemala has dragged on for more than 35 years, causing some 100,000 deaths. Another 40,000 civilians are said to have disappeared and human rights groups have accused the army of grave abuses against civilians.
Details of the accord were not immediately available but Notimex said talks on the next stage, reintegrating the guerrillas into civilian life, would begin later this month.
The agreement was expected to be signed in Madrid later this year, with a ceasefire sealed in Oslo before yearend.
